instruction: Open the provided init.ifc wall shell in Bonsai. Add hosted door and window openings, save the completed IFC4 model as result.ifc, and export a door/window schedule as result.csv using a Bonsai or IfcCSV-style workflow. The result should contain one project, one building storey, four walls, one slab, two doors, three windows, five opening elements, five void relationships, and five fill relationships. Do not include building element proxies or furnishing elements. Every door and window must fill exactly one opening, and each of those openings must void an IfcWall. The CSV must use the exact header order GlobalId, Class, TypeName, Width, Height, HostWall. It should contain exactly five data rows with unique GlobalId values matching the IfcDoor or IfcWindow elements in result.ifc, with the same class and hosted wall name. Include these records in any row order, with Width and Height within 0.05 m: IfcDoor DoorType-1000 Width 1.0 Height 2.1 HostWall Wall-S; IfcDoor DoorType-1000 Width 1.0 Height 2.1 HostWall Wall-N; IfcWindow WindowType-1200 Width 1.2 Height 1.2 HostWall Wall-N; a second IfcWindow WindowType-1200 Width 1.2 Height 1.2 HostWall Wall-N; and IfcWindow WindowType-1000 Width 1.0 Height 1.2 HostWall Wall-E. Other details may vary.
